title: Sample 19-3: Coded Letter Puzzle

illustrates.quote: e. Use uncontracted braille when coded puzzles are scrambled letters. f. Grade 1 indicators may be required before single letters in the puzzle or key.

blocks.text: Decode the words from your spelling list using the secret code. Write your answer in the space provided.
blocks.features: Given braille (lines 1-3) shows a uniform indent on every line — built blocked:true.

blocks.features: A QWERTY-keyboard-to-alphabet substitution key, boxed and wrapped in one continuous grade-1 passage (so no per-letter grade-1 indicators are needed inside it, unlike 19.2.2f's own per-letter case — confirmed: none of the given braille's key rows carry a ';' symbol indicator). Column alignment (letter directly under its own code letter) is not reproducible (F-219).

Five scrambled/coded spelling words, each in UNCONTRACTED braille per 19.3.1e (backtick-marked here so buildModel19 builds a genuine `uncontracted:true` segment, matching F-218's positive finding) — confirmed uncontracted directly from the given braille: 'usqll' keeps its double-l spelled out rather than contracting to the 'll' group sign, which grade-2 would otherwise apply.

print.notes: An instruction paragraph, a QWERTY-keyboard code key (boxed), and five numbered scrambled-letter puzzle words in uncontracted braille.
